title_en: Ji Qing Company and Hua Ding Company v. Agricultural Bank of China Tibet Branch Business Department — dispute over mortgage loan contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, which provides that 'where one or both parties consist of two or more persons, and the subject matter of the action is common, or the subject matter is of the same category, and the people's court considers that the cases may be consolidated for trial and the parties agree, such shall constitute a joint action,' is a provision that requires the consent of the parties for consolidation of claims based on multiple parties. Its precondition is that one or both parties must consist of two or more persons. Chinese law has no mandatory requirement that consolidation of claims based on multiple subject matters must obtain the consent of the parties. Where a creditor files a single lawsuit for two matured debts, the people's court's consolidation of the cases for trial and issuance of a single judgment does not violate legal provisions.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. Jiqing Company and Huading Company v. Agricultural Bank of China Tibet Branch Business Department
— Dispute over Mortgage Loan Contract

【Ruling Summary】

Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law provides: "If one party or both parties consist of two or more persons, and the subject matter of the action is common, or the subject matter of the action is of the same category, and the People's Court deems that consolidation of trial is possible and the parties consent, it shall be a joint action." This provision is a stipulation regarding consolidation of trial of multiple parties, which requires the consent of the parties, and its premise is that one party or both parties must consist of two or more persons. There is no mandatory provision in Chinese law requiring the consent of the parties for consolidation of trial of multiple subject matters. Where a creditor initiates an action jointly for two matured debts, and the People's Court consolidates the trial and renders a single judgment, it does not violate legal provisions.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 186

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Tibet Jiqing Industrial Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 14 Zhaji Road, Lhasa City, Tibet Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Wang Weimin, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Chang Xiaorun, lawyer of Beijing Tianmu Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Agricultural Bank of China Tibet Autonomous Region Branch Business Department, domiciled at No. 103 Linkuo East Road, Lhasa City, Tibet Autonomous Region.
Person in Charge: Zhaxi Pingcuo, General Manager of the Business Department.
Agent ad litem: Baima, lawyer of Tibet Xueyu Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Li Jianzhong, lawyer of Tibet Xueyu Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Chongqing Huading Modern Agricultural Landscape Park Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dazhong Village, Yudong Town, Banan District, Chongqing City.
Legal Representative: Huang Xiuqin, General Manager.
Agent ad litem: Gao Heyong, Financial Manager of the Company.

The appellant, Tibet Jiqing Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiqing Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2005) Zang Min Er Chu Zi No. 01 rendered by the High People's Court of Tibet Autonomous Region in the case of dispute over mortgage loan contract between it and the appellee, Agricultural Bank of China Tibet Autonomous Region Branch Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department), and the defendant at first instance, Chongqing Huading Modern Agricultural Landscape Park Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huading Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with trial judge Wu Qingbao as presiding judge, and assistant judges Gong Bangyou and Liu Min as members, to conduct the trial, with court clerk Zhao Suijun serving as the recorder. The present case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found: On August 6, 2001, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department entered into a Loan Contract and a Mortgage Contract with Jiqing Company and Huading Company, respectively. The Loan Contract stipulated that the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department would grant a loan of RMB 20 million to Jiqing Company, with a loan term of two years, an annual interest rate of 5.94%, and quarterly interest settlement; if Jiqing Company's default caused the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department to resort to litigation to realize its claims, Jiqing Company should bear the lawyer fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims paid by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department for that purpose. The Mortgage Contract stipulated that Huading Company would provide a guarantee for this RMB 20 million loan with the land use right of the "Modern Agricultural Demonstration Zone" in Zhongba, Yudong Town, Banan District, Chongqing City. On August 6, 2003, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department, Jiqing Company, and Huading Company entered into a Loan Extension Agreement, stipulating that the loan term would be extended for one year, i.e., from August 6, 2003 to August 6, 2004.

On December 22, 2003, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department again entered into a Loan Contract and a Mortgage Contract with Jiqing Company and Huading Company, respectively. The Loan Contract stipulated that the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department would grant a loan of RMB 27 million to Jiqing Company, with a loan term of one year, an annual interest rate of 3.33%, and quarterly interest settlement; if Jiqing Company's default caused the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department to resort to litigation to realize its claims, Jiqing Company should bear the lawyer fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims paid by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department for that purpose. The Mortgage Contract stipulated that Huading Company would provide a guarantee for this RMB 27 million loan with the land use right of the "Modern Agricultural Demonstration Zone" in Zhongba, Yudong Town, Banan District, Chongqing City.

It was further found that: On December 30, 2002, the Tibet Autonomous Region Price Bureau and the Tibet Autonomous Region Department of Justice jointly issued the "Tibet Autonomous Region Lawyer Service Fee Standards (Trial)", which established standards for lawyer fees in cases involving property relations, namely: RMB 10 million to RMB 50 million, fees are taken at 2% to 2.5%.

After the two loans totaling RMB 47 million matured, Jiqing Company failed to repay them. On February 28, 2005, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department filed a lawsuit with the High People's Court of Tibet Autonomous Region, requesting a judgment ordering Jiqing Company to repay the principal amounts of RMB 47 million and corresponding interest, penalty interest, overdue interest, etc., and to bear the lawyer fees, travel expenses, preservation fees, and litigation costs it incurred for realizing its claims; and Huading Company to assume the guaranty liability for the above debts and costs with the mortgaged property.

On March 1, 2005, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department applied to the court for property preservation. On March 8, 2005, the court issued a civil ruling (2005) Zang Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 1, sealing up 14,266.05 square meters of land under the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" Chuan Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 00058 of the respondent, Jiqing Company, located at Group 8, Zongshu Village, South Railway Station Subdistrict, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

During the trial at first instance, Jiqing Company repaid RMB 5 million of the loan principal and RMB 2 million of the interest on May 24, 2005 and June 3, 2005, respectively.

The court of first instance held: The Loan Contract and Mortgage Contract respectively entered into by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department with Jiqing Company and Huading Company were expressions of mutual intent reached through equal negotiation, lawfully established, and legally valid. The claim of the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department for a judgment ordering Jiqing Company to repay RMB 49,309,369.91 and Huading Company to assume the guaranty liability was in accordance with the law, Jiqing Company and Huading Company also admitted the debt amount, and the court supported it. As to the defendants' defense that the plaintiff's lawyer fees had not been actually paid, the court held that lawyer fees were explicitly agreed upon in the Loan Contract and represented the true intent of the parties. Due to Jiqing Company's default, lawyer fees were inevitable when the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department entrusted lawyers to realize its rights through litigation. Therefore, the court did not support the defense of the two defendants. According to the provisions of the Tibet price department on the range of lawyer fees, combined with the subject matter of the case and the actual workload undertaken by the lawyers, the court considered that the lawyer agency fee should be set at 2% of the principal of RMB 47 million, which is the lower limit. Pursuant to Articles 8, 111(1), 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 57 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment was rendered as follows: 1. Jiqing Company shall repay the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department the loan principal of RMB 47 million and interest of RMB 2,309,369.94, minus the RMB 7 million already paid during the trial (RMB 5 million principal, RMB 2 million interest), Jiqing Company still needs to pay the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department principal of RMB 42 million and interest of RMB 309,369.94, totaling principal and interest of RMB 42,309,369.94; from April 26, 2005, Jiqing Company shall also pay overdue liquidated damages to the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department at a daily rate of 0.021% until all principal and interest are paid off. 2. Jiqing Company shall bear the lawyer agency fee of RMB 940,000 for the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department's litigation, but the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department shall provide payment vouchers to Jiqing Company. 3. The case acceptance fee and property preservation fee totaling RMB 489,281 shall be borne by Jiqing Company. 4. Huading Company shall assume joint and several liability for the debts and costs in items 1, 2, and 3 above with the mortgaged land use right. 5. After Huading Company actually assumes joint and several liability, it has the right to seek recourse from Jiqing Company.

Jiqing Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the High People's Court of Tibet Autonomous Region, appealed to this Court, contending: First, the two loan guarantee contracts it entered into with the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department, due to differences in loan time, amount, term, and interest rate, constituted two different legal relationships. The Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department should have brought separate lawsuits based on these two legal relationships. The court of first instance not only consolidated the trial of these two different lawsuits but also rendered a single judgment, violating legal procedures and should be remanded for retrial. Second, regarding the burden of lawyer fees, there is no clear legal provision. Generally, courts do not support a party's claim for lawyer fees. Even according to the Loan Contract provision that "if the borrower's default causes the lender to resort to litigation to realize its claims, the borrower shall bear the lawyer fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims paid by the lender for that purpose," Jiqing Company should bear the lawyer fees actually paid by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department due to the litigation. In this case, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department neither provided the agency contract it entered into with the law firm nor the receipts for payment of lawyer fees to the law firm, thus failing to prove the basic fact of losses suffered by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department due to Jiqing Company's default and the true amount of losses. The lawyer fee of RMB 940,000 awarded by the court of first instance had not actually occurred. Moreover, the legal relationship in this case is not complex, and the workload of the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department's agent lawyer was very small. The fee standard in the "Tibet Autonomous Region Lawyer Service Fee Standards (Trial)" relied upon by the court of first instance is clearly too high. The judgment of the court of first instance lacks factual and legal basis and should be corrected. Third, the total subject matter of this case is less than RMB 50 million, and Huading Company also provided a mortgage guarantee of land use rights worth over RMB 70 million. The court of first instance's ruling to seal up Jiqing Company's 14,266.05 square meters of land use rights exceeded the litigation subject matter, causing huge operational difficulties and economic losses to Jiqing Company. The property seized in excess of the subject matter should be released from seizure. Request to set aside the judgment of first instance and remand the case to the court of first instance for retrial; and for the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department to bear the litigation costs.

The appellee, Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department, replied: First, although the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department entered into two loan contracts with Jiqing Company, constituting two legal facts, both loans had matured, and only one creditor-debtor legal relationship existed between the parties. There were no multiple or different legal relationships. The Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department's filing of a lawsuit to realize its claims was not improper. Jiqing Company's view that separate lawsuits should be brought lacks legal basis. Second, the court of first instance's judgment that Jiqing Company bear the lawyer fee of RMB 940,000 was well-founded, reasonable, and lawful. The agreement between the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department and Jiqing Company in the Loan Contract that "if the borrower's default causes the lender to resort to litigation to realize its claims, the borrower shall bear the lawyer fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims paid by the lender for that purpose" was voluntarily negotiated by the parties and should be protected by law. Given that Jiqing Company failed to repay the loan in accordance with the contract, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department realized its claims through litigation, and the resulting lawyer fees were inevitable. Moreover, to avoid increasing Jiqing Company's burden and to achieve fairness, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department agreed with its agent lawyer to pay lawyer fees in accordance with the fee-taking standards of the "Tibet Autonomous Region Lawyer Service Fee Standards (Trial)". In its claim at first instance, it argued for the lawyer fee to be borne based on the segmented fee-taking ratio of 2% to 2.5% under that standard. The court of first instance's adoption of the lower limit of 2% of the RMB 47 million principal was fair and reasonable to Jiqing Company. Third, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department's legal application for seizure of the appellee's land use rights did not clearly exceed the value. The court of first instance's findings of fact were clear and the application of law was correct. Request to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

The court of second instance, in addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, also found: During the trial at first instance, no agency contract was entered into between the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department and its agent law firm, Tibet Xueyu Law Firm (hereinafter referred to as Xueyu Law Firm), nor were agency fees actually paid. At the second instance trial, the agent of the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department stated that the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department had verbally agreed with Xueyu Law Firm to pay after the case was concluded. After the judgment of first instance, on September 30, 2005, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department paid the lawyer agency fee of RMB 940,000 as specified in the judgment of first instance to Xueyu Law Firm. During the second instance, lawyers Baima and Li Jianzhong of Xueyu Law Firm submitted to this Court the "Contract for Retaining Permanent Legal Counsel" entered into between the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department and Xueyu Law Firm, effective from September 5, 2004 to September 4, 2007, which stated: Upon the client's request, the retained party designates lawyers Baima and Li Jianzhong as the permanent legal counsel of the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department; the annual legal counsel fee is X yuan; the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department's entrustment of legal counsel to represent litigation, participate in mediation, or arbitration activities shall be charged separately. Fees must strictly reflect the principle of contingency fees. The scope of contingency fee cases is expanded to all cases. For cases with contingency fees, the lawyer's agency work shall be responsible until the enforcement of the case is concluded or the creditor's rights are satisfied. The calculation method for lawyer fees in contingency fee cases is: the amount of property recovered or saved multiplied by the fee-taking ratio of the corresponding level (fee-taking ratio details refer to the "Lawyer Professional Fee Standards"), etc. During the second instance, the agents lawyers Baima and Li Jianzhong of the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department also submitted to this Court evidence of some travel expenses during the second instance and the second instance "Agency (Defense) Contract" entered into between the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department and Xueyu Law Firm. That "Agency (Defense) Contract" stipulated that the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department shall pay labor remuneration of RMB 470,000 to Xueyu Law Firm, and the second instance agency fee shall be paid by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department in a lump sum to Xueyu Law Firm upon receipt of the second instance judgment or ruling.

This Court, upon trial, holds: Although the RMB 47 million debt claimed by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department in this case originally arose from two loan contracts, given that both loans had matured when it filed the lawsuit with the High People's Court of Tibet Autonomous Region, its filing of a single lawsuit does not violate mandatory legal provisions. The joint action under Article 53 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which requires the consent of the parties for the People's Court to consolidate trial, refers to the consolidation of multiple parties. Its premise is that one party or both parties consist of two or more persons. In this case, one party and the other party each consist of one person, so there is no issue of consolidation of multiple parties; rather, it is a factual consolidation of multiple subject matters. Since Chinese law does not require the consent of the parties as a prerequisite for consolidation of trial of multiple subject matters in a joint action, the court of first instance's consolidation of the trial of the debts arising from the two contracts into a single judgment based on the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department's claim was not improper. This Court does not support Jiqing Company's appeal request that the court of first instance violated legal procedures and should remand the case for retrial.

Regarding the burden of lawyer agency fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims, because Article 5 of the Loan Contract entered into between the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department and Jiqing Company explicitly stipulates: "If the borrower's default causes the lender to resort to litigation to realize its claims, the borrower shall bear the lawyer fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims paid by the lender for that purpose." This stipulation represents the true intent of the parties and does not violate prohibitive legal provisions, therefore it is valid. The People's Court shall protect, in accordance with the law, the lawyer fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims actually paid by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department to realize this claim. When the creditor, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department, filed the lawsuit with the High People's Court of Tibet Autonomous Region, although it had already retained lawyers from Xueyu Law Firm to participate in the litigation, it had not entered into an agency contract with Xueyu Law Firm regarding the agency matter, and had not actually paid the lawyer agency fee. Therefore, the court of first instance's determination that Jiqing Company should bear, according to the Loan Contract, the first instance agency fee paid by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department to realize its claims lacked corresponding factual basis. The amount of lawyer agency fees should be determined based on the agreement between the principal and the law firm. In the absence of an agreement between the principal Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department and Xueyu Law Firm, the court of first instance's own determination based on the "Tibet Autonomous Region Lawyer Service Fee Standards (Trial)" lacked legal basis, and this Court does not recognize it. Furthermore, from the content of the "Contract for Retaining Permanent Legal Counsel" effective from September 5, 2004 to September 4, 2007, between Xueyu Law Firm and the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department, which stated: "The Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department's entrustment of legal counsel to represent litigation, participate in mediation, or arbitration activities shall be charged separately. Fees must strictly reflect the principle of contingency fees. The scope of contingency fee cases is expanded to all cases. For cases with contingency fees, the lawyer's agency work shall be responsible until the enforcement of the case is concluded or the creditor's rights are satisfied. The calculation method for lawyer fees in contingency fee cases is: the amount of property recovered or saved multiplied by the fee-taking ratio of the corresponding level (fee-taking ratio details refer to the 'Lawyer Professional Fee Standards')," it can be seen that normally, the parties would calculate the lawyer agency fee based on the amount of property recovered or saved at the time of final conclusion of enforcement or satisfaction of creditor's rights. Since this case is still under second instance trial, and the amount of property ultimately recoverable by the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department is not yet finally determined, there is no valid basis for determining the lawyer agency fee. Moreover, other travel expenses and costs of realizing claims may continue to occur because the case is not yet finally concluded and enforcement is not complete. Therefore, this case only determines the loan legal relationship. As for the lawyer fees, travel expenses, and other costs of realizing claims, after the case is finally enforced, the Agricultural Bank Tibet Branch Business Department may separately claim based on the actual situation. This case does not make a determination on this matter.

Jiqing Company's appeal request that the court of first instance's seizure exceeding the subject matter should be lifted is not within the scope of appeal against the judgment of first instance, so this Court does not address it.

Pursuant to Article 8 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 53(1), Article 140, Article 153(1)(1) and (3), and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm items 1, 3, and 5 of the main text of the civil judgment (2005) Zang Min Er Chu Zi No. 01 of the High People's Court of Tibet Autonomous Region;

2. Set aside item 2 of the said civil judgment;

3. Amend item 4 of the said civil judgment to read: Chongqing Huading Modern Agricultural Landscape Park Development Co., Ltd. shall assume joint and several liability for the loan principal and interest, case acceptance fee, and property preservation fee to be borne by Tibet Jiqing Industrial Development Co., Ltd. with the mortgaged land use right.

The aforesaid amounts payable shall be satisfied within 10 days from the day following the service of this judgment. In case of delay, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 244,641, of which Tibet Jiqing Industrial Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 200,000, and the Business Department of the Tibet Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China shall bear RMB 44,641.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wu Qingbao

Acting Judge: Gong Bangyou

Acting Judge: Liu Min

December 8, 2005

Clerk: Zhao Suijun

【Profile of the Presiding Judge】

Wu Qingbao, Senior Judge: born in 1964, Bachelor of Laws. Served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2001.
